task.description:
RE-GATE after rework iteration 1. Your prior FAIL (this same handoff, now superseded below) found the SET search_path fixture technique in test/letflow/identity/user_test.exs, group_test.exs, tenant_role_test.exs, and role_registry_test.exs was not rollback-safe. TEST-DESIGNER's rework report (handoffs/WF02-REQ063-20260818/step-03-test-designer.json) claims it applied your required_fix option (a) (mirroring identity_test.exs's mode-restore sequence), but ALSO reports that doing so exactly as directed surfaced a SECOND bug your own review didn't anticipate: {:shared, self()} mode ties connection ownership to the test process, and on_exit (running in ExUnit.OnExitHandler, a different process) force-switching the pool back to :auto to run its own DROP SCHEMA/DELETE cleanup allegedly raced against that ownership teardown, leaving orphaned req063-* tenant rows in public.tenants across runs. TEST-DESIGNER's claimed fix for THIS second issue: switched from {:shared, self()} to plain :manual mode + a bare checkout, checked back in via an explicit Sandbox.checkin/1 registered in on_exit (same-process checkin/checkout, no cross-process handoff).

Your job: independently verify this second claim too, not just re-check the original fix. Read deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/adapters/sql/sandbox.ex's own documentation on Sandbox.checkin/1 and on cross-process mode-switching to confirm the race TEST-DESIGNER describes is real and that their fix (explicit same-process checkin in on_exit, no {:shared, self()}) actually closes it -- don't just accept the narrative. Read all four fixed files directly. Run the full suite yourself at least twice (TEST-DESIGNER's own verification found a run-3 failure in ONE of their 4 runs, in a file this rework never touched -- Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatusTest, traced to a pre-existing flake already referenced by ISS-0031/GH#90 -- confirm this attribution is correct and not a symptom you should instead trace back to the search_path fix). Also spot-check user_test.exs's restructured 'two different tenant schemas' test (TEST-DESIGNER reports splitting the fixture helper into provision_tenant_schema!/0 and point_search_path_at!/1 and changing this test's provisioning strategy) still actually asserts what REQ-063's acceptance criterion requires (two users, same username, two different tenant schemas, no conflict).

Do a real Postgres row-count check yourself for leftover req063-*/orphaned tenant rows after running the suite, matching the verification TEST-DESIGNER claims to have done -- don't just trust their reported row counts.

Original Step 3b instructions below, still applicable for anything not superseded above: Independently validate TEST-DESIGNER's work. Read test/specs/REQ-063.md and the actual test source files directly -- do not read TEST-DESIGNER's handoff result.summary as a substitute.

This run has an unusual wrinkle worth extra scrutiny: TEST-DESIGNER's own report describes fixing several test files (test/letflow/identity/user_test.exs, group_test.exs, tenant_role_test.exs, test/letflow/role_registry_test.exs) via a `SET search_path TO "<schema>", public` technique, used because RoleRegistry and some bare-struct inserts have no `prefix:` call site of their own. Scrutinize this specifically: (a) is this a real, sound technique for a test fixture, or does it risk leaking search_path state across tests sharing a sandboxed connection (check Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox's checkout/checkin behavior -- does a SET search_path survive past this test's own transaction rollback, could it bleed into an unrelated test on the same connection)? (b) is it used ONLY where genuinely necessary (no prefix: call site exists) or was it used as a shortcut somewhere prefix: threading was actually available and should have been used instead? TEST-DESIGNER's own handoff claims this was 'verified transaction-scoped/rollback-safe against real Postgres before adopting it' -- confirm this claim yourself rather than accepting it.

Also specifically verify: (1) all ~39 previously-failing tests are genuinely fixed, not skipped/excluded -- grep for @tag :skip or excluded tests in the touched files; (2) the new test/letflow/identity_migration_test.exs's drop-migration guard-skip test actually runs the real shipped migration (Ecto.Migrator.run/4 against the actual file), not a reimplementation of its logic in Elixir that could drift from the real SQL; (3) the cross-tenant username-collision test and the (external_realm,external_id)-cross-tenant-rejection test both exist and assert against real DB constraint violations, not mocked; (4) test fixtures use per-test unique data (grep for hardcoded tenant/schema names shared across tests); (5) docs/issues/ISS-0047.yaml (the independently-found insert_or_fetch/4 username-race bug) is legitimately out of scope for THIS run to fix -- confirm it's correctly filed as a separate, pre-existing, non-blocking issue rather than something masking a REQ-063 acceptance criterion.

result.summary:
RE-GATE FAIL. Original iteration-1 BLOCKER (SET search_path leaking outside a real sandboxed transaction) is genuinely fixed -- confirmed by reading all four files and by 3 of my own full-suite runs (770/770, 770/770, 770/770) plus a real Postgres row-count check after each run (0 leftover req063-* tenant rows every time; the one stray tenant_%% schema present throughout was pre-existing, tied to zero tenant rows, unrelated to this fix). The run-3 TenantStatusTest flake attribution to ISS-0031/GH#90 is independently confirmed correct: that file is async: true, uses an unfiltered node-global :telemetry.attach handler that fires synchronously in whichever process's query triggers it (not scoped to the attaching test's own process), and ISS-0031's own record documents this exact mechanism pre-dating REQ-063 -- none of my 3 runs even hit this flake, and it is structurally unrelated to Sandbox mode-switching in the four rework files (which are all async: false, never running concurrently with anything).

The BLOCKER is TEST-DESIGNER's second-bug fix mechanism itself, not its observed outcome. Read deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/adapters/sql/sandbox.ex and deps/db_connection/lib/db_connection/ownership/manager.ex directly, then empirically verified with two standalone probe scripts (run via `mix run` against the real Docker Postgres, not just source-reading) in scratch/checkin_probe.exs and scratch/checkin_probe2.exs: Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.checkin/1, called from a process OTHER than the one that ran checkout/2, returns :not_found -- a silent no-op, not a real checkin (confirmed via DBConnection.Ownership.Manager.handle_call(:checkin, {caller, _}, state)'s own proxy_checkin(state, caller, caller) -- it only ever checks in a connection keyed by the CALLING process's own pid). ExUnit.OnExitHandler's own source (on_exit_handler.ex, ships with Elixir at C:/Program Files/Elixir/lib/ex_unit) confirms on_exit/1 callbacks run via spawn_monitor in a dedicated runner process, never the test process that did the checkout. So the fix all four files now ship -- 'Sandbox.mode(Repo, :manual) + checkout, checked back in via an explicit Sandbox.checkin/1 registered in on_exit' -- registers a checkin call that is ALWAYS a no-op in practice, not the 'same-process checkin/checkout, no cross-process handoff' the task description and every one of the four files' moduledocs claim. My probe #2 also showed why no leak is actually observed: when the owning (test) process dies, DBConnection.Ownership.Manager's own :DOWN monitor (handle_info({:DOWN, ref, _, _, _}, state), unconditional, not mode-dependent) already reclaims the connection automatically -- this is the same safety net that protected the ORIGINAL {:shared, self()} code too (owner_down/unshare fire on :DOWN regardless of shared vs manual mode), which casts real doubt on whether the reported 69-row leak was actually caused by the diagnosed 'cross-process on_exit mode-force race' at all, versus some other transient cause never isolated. identity_test.exs's own established, actually-correct pattern (lines 278-354) does the mode restore INLINE IN THE TEST BODY, in the same process, before that process exits -- not deferred into on_exit -- which is why it works for a reason unrelated to what the four rework files' moduledocs now claim.

Net effect: the observed test behavior (no leak, 770/770 x3) is fine, but the checked-in fix ships four moduledocs asserting a false claim about Ecto Sandbox's own documented semantics ('Explicit checkin avoids that race entirely: the same process that checked the connection out also checks it back in' -- user_test.exs line 58-60, mirrored near-verbatim in the other three) as permanent project documentation, and the actual protection mechanism (process-death auto-reclaim, which was already present pre-rework) is never named. This is exactly the kind of unverified-claim-as-fact this gate exists to catch, per core-directives.md's No Speculation rule -- 'confirmed empirically' language throughout TEST-DESIGNER's report and the moduledocs does not hold up under independent re-derivation.

issues.summary: All four files' (user_test.exs, group_test.exs, tenant_role_test.exs, role_registry_test.exs) on_exit-registered Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.checkin(Letflow.Repo) call is a no-op: on_exit/1 callbacks run in a separate ExUnit.OnExitHandler-spawned process, and Sandbox.checkin/1 only checks in a connection owned by the CALLING process (confirmed via deps/db_connection/lib/db_connection/ownership/manager.ex's proxy_checkin(state, caller, caller) and empirically via scratch/checkin_probe.exs / checkin_probe2.exs against real Postgres -- checkin from a non-owning process returns :not_found every time). The moduledoc claim in all four files ('the same process that checked the connection out also checks it back in') is false as written. Required fix: either (a) do the mode-restore-to-:auto/cleanup INLINE in the test body before the test process exits, mirroring identity_test.exs's own actually-correct concurrent-race test (lines 278-354 there), removing the on_exit-based checkin entirely, or (b) if keeping an on_exit-based cleanup step, correct the moduledoc to state the real protection mechanism (DBConnection.Ownership.Manager's unconditional :DOWN-monitor reclaim on owning-process death, deps/db_connection/lib/db_connection/ownership/manager.ex handle_info({:DOWN,...)) instead of the false claim, and re-verify that whichever mechanism is actually documented is the one actually preventing the leak (not simply that no leak was observed, which the untouched :DOWN-based reclaim already explains on its own).
